The relay sees who is asking and not what; the proxy sees what and not who. No independent relay exists yet, so this path is not in use. Either way, the RPC provider behind the proxy sees every query, coming from the proxy.

To receive, a wallet tries to decrypt the encrypted note beside every new commitment in the pool. That costs one X25519 operation per output, then one cheap attempt per key: the wallet’s own, the plain one, and one for each payment code it is looking for. There are no view tags. What this version does not protect

What you choose on this site is kept in your browser’s localStorage, on your device, and is never sent anywhere: the palette you picked (dusk or night), and the address of your own RPC endpoint if you saved one. Clearing this site’s data in your browser removes it.
What you paste stays in this page. To check it, the page reads the transactions it names from

Where a page may connect is a second rule. Because you can point the scanner at an RPC endpoint of your own, the policy sent with the page has to allow a connection to any https address. As a page loads, this site’s own script adds a narrower rule: this site, the one RPC endpoint in use and the waitlist, nothing else. The browser enforces that rule too, it cannot be loosened again until the page is reloaded, and the scanner does not start without it. It is put there by the site’s own script, so it guards against a mistake in this site, not against a copy of the site that someone has changed.
